The strongest ground is that the promise violates the statute of frauds: a promise to pay a debt that the statute of limitations has barred must be in a signed writing to be enforceable, and this one was oral. The barred debt is a weaker ground, because a new promise can revive a time-barred debt without new consideration under Restatement (Second) of Contracts § 82. The overheard "deadbeat" remark is a distractor that doesn't supply duress or consideration.

CONFIDENCE: 72
